newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel investigates grants to Murdoch company.
newsitem.headline: Israel investigates grants to Murdoch company.

text.p: The Israeli government's Investment Centre said on Monday it is investigating grants given to a Jerusalem-based company controlled by media magnate Rupert Murdoch.

David Baruch, director of the centre, which provides subsidies to companies building or expanding factories in Israel, said the investigations concerned $1.5 million in grants given in 1992 and 1993 to News Datacom Research Ltd, a wholly owned Israeli subsidiary of Murdoch's News Corp.
An additional request for $8 million in aid made this year has not been brought up for review yet, Baruch said. The aid is provided to companies producing products for export.

Meanwhile, the Income Tax Authority said it was questioning five people connected with News Datacom Research. The company is suspected of concealing up to $150 million in income earned between 1989 and 1996.
In a statement, the authority said "those under investigation were cooperating with investigators". It did not name the five and a spokeswoman for the authority would not reveal further details.
"It should be stressed that as of now no arrests have been made and that we have no reason to make any arrests," the authority said.

News Datacom Research sources said that to their knowledge all the company's products were produced by its U.K. parent company, also called News Datacom, and sold from there. They said News Datcom Research was only a research and development operation.
News Datacom develops and sells encryption systems mainly for pay television broadcasters, like Murdoch's SKY Television.

The tax investigation, which the Income Tax Authority said is one of the largest in Israel's history, has been under way for several months. On Sunday scores of investigators descended on News Datacom Research's Jerusalem headquarters, removing boxes of documents.

They also took documents from the offices of Herzog Fox Ne'eman and Yigal Arnon, two of the country's most prestigious law firms. But the documents from the law firms have not been opened by investigators, due to laws protecting lawyer-client confidentiality, pending a court ruling permitting them to do so.
